criteria.rationale: No bundle, attestation or schema changes. Closed scopes that verify reported superseded now report closed, matching what review-check already said; the one tightening is that a closed scope whose newest attestation rejects or requests changes is no longer approved through an older approval, which only removes a false pass. Open scopes and changed federated manifests behave as before, the latter pinned by the existing revocation test.

The helper comment names both routine causes of supersession (closeout-commit provenance and new matrix checks), why federation read the stricter answer, and the preserved legacy-evidence waiver. The spec records the measurement at both pins, the regression the full suite caught, and the two proofs against the defect. The changelog fragment states the user-visible effect for consumers.

Pinning a newer engine no longer requires resealing and reattesting every consumed upstream scope; the last pin needed 28. Measured on this repository: the ABM sources and the multirepo foundation verify closed at c5c029c, and Harne8's closeout-check for harne8-abm-governed-execution is terminal. verify keeps reporting the delta and names the retention in a warning, so an operator still sees what changed since the review.

One shared helper, its use in review-check and verify, the manifest guard and one test file with its producer. Narrowing the sealed matrix was considered and rejected in the spec because the closeout commit alone supersedes a bundle.

Retention requires the newest attested bundle's attestation to pass the full attestation validation, including decision, authority and evidence rules, so a later rejection wins. A changed federated manifest disables retention, so revoked trust or an unauthorized or moved source still stales a closed scope; TestFederatedRoadmapMilestoneBundleSealsOwnManifestAndKeepsLegacySeals caught the first version that allowed it and passes now.
